title: The Science of Sleep Cycles: Why You Wake Up Tired

slides.heading: Why You Wake Up Tired
slides.body: The science behind sleep cycles — and how to finally feel rested

slides.heading: Sleep Is Not One Thing
slides.body: Sleep isn't a single continuous state. Your brain cycles through distinct stages all night long, each serving a different biological purpose. Missing any stage has consequences you feel the next day.

slides.heading: The 90-Minute Cycle
slides.body: One complete sleep cycle lasts roughly 90 minutes and repeats 4–6 times per night. Each cycle moves through light sleep, deep sleep, and REM. Waking mid-cycle — not at the end — is the #1 reason you feel groggy.

slides.heading: Stage 1 & 2: Light Sleep
slides.body: You spend about 50% of the night in light sleep. Your body temperature drops, heart rate slows, and your brain produces sleep spindles — bursts of activity that consolidate memories. This is the easiest stage to wake from.

slides.heading: Stage 3: Deep Sleep (Slow-Wave)
slides.body: Deep sleep is when your body does most of its physical repair: growth hormone is released, immune cells multiply, and tissues rebuild. Just 20% of your night, but it determines how physically restored you feel.

slides.heading: REM: The Dream Stage
slides.body: Rapid Eye Movement sleep is when your brain is nearly as active as when awake. It processes emotions, strengthens creative connections, and clears metabolic waste via the glymphatic system. Most REM happens in the final hours of sleep.

slides.heading: Why Alarm Clocks Are the Enemy
slides.body: Alarms cut cycles short — often during deep or REM sleep — triggering sleep inertia: the foggy, disoriented feeling that can last up to 90 minutes. Your brain was mid-process and gets yanked out unexpectedly.

slides.heading: Alcohol Ruins Your REM
slides.body: Alcohol helps you fall asleep faster but suppresses REM sleep in the first half of the night. As it metabolizes, your brain rebounds with fragmented, lighter sleep. You sleep 8 hours yet still feel exhausted.

slides.heading: The 90-Minute Hack
slides.body: Time your sleep in 90-minute multiples: 6 hours (4 cycles) or 7.5 hours (5 cycles) often feels better than 8 hours interrupted mid-cycle. Apps like Sleep Cycle track movement to wake you at the lightest phase.

slides.heading: Sleep Smarter, Not Longer
slides.body: Quality beats quantity. Consistent bedtimes, avoiding alcohol before sleep, and waking at cycle boundaries can transform how rested you feel — no extra hours needed.
